item.title: Cybersecurity Reading List
item.description:
I hope to create dedicated pages for the most notable of entries on this list, but for now just need a place to quickly jot them all down.

Books

While I tend to prefer nonfiction titles for this genre, there are some notable works of fiction that I feel are good reads for interested parties to be familiar with as well.

Nonfiction

  • Hackers: Heroes of the Computer Revolution by Steven Levy, 1984. A series of stories about the people who created modern computing.

item.title: Hackers - Heroes of the Computer Revolution
item.description: An essential anthology for anyone wanting to learn about the origins of modern computing. Originally published in 1984, this book chronicles multiple groups dating back to the 1950s, the people who forged the original profile of the hacker. This book focuses on creators of early personal computing kits (Steve Wozniak and Lee Felsenstein), Ted Hoff, the designer of the legendary Intel 4004 microprocessor, and Stewart Brand, the publisher of The Whole Earth Catalog.

item.title: Ghost in the Shell (1995)
item.description: Written before the mass adoption of the internet, before the social and technological terms we all are now comfortable with (and in many cases were born into). This is a story about a law enforcement team on the cutting edge of what the 80s thought today’s tech was going to be like. Cybernetic implants, smart tracker bullets, remote mind wipes, optical camouflage, the works. The story chronicles inter-agency turf wars played at the highest level, and the emergency of a new kind of criminal. It does this while asking deep questions about what it means to be a human, a distinct person, in a connection and increasingly synthetic world.

item.title: The Cuckoos Egg
item.description: The Cuckoo’s Egg is the autobiographical account of an astronomy student who’s grant ran out so he got a job in the university’s IT department. A 75 cent discrepancy in the accounting software would lead him down a rabbit hole of hackers, military and national security systems, and academia. This all being told from the author’s experiences it is a fascinating tale of the very real world of cyber security in the twilight years of the Cold War.

item.title: Ghost in the Shell (2026)
item.description:
Oh man, I had really high hopes from the trailer. I had high hopes.

The opening text went by at blink and you miss it speed. Luckily, it was faithfully pulled from the original manga, which was sitting on the bookshelf next to me. And that was the tone throughout. On one had you get a highly faithful rendering of the source material, while simultaneously it is being warped in odd ways that I did not care for. Muted color space and textures on a gritty realistic background, but saturated and vibrant color on characters who art style would seamlessly ramp from 1990s anime to (what I think of as) Rick and Morty and back again. It was jarring and made it impossible to fully sit in the material and enjoy the show.
